_comment: Retirements of GENERATED per-project artifacts - the cleanup the upstream file compare can never name, because generated output was never a stack-shipped file. The update command applies these (with the same one-gate consent as its prune list) and validate flags them; detection is existence-based, never version math, so a leftover is caught no matter how old the install. `unwire_settings_hook` names the hook file whose settings.json entry goes, optionally scoped to one matcher as `<file>::<Matcher>` when the file stays wired for its other events. Paths resolve against the install root (the project's .claude/ parent, or the account dir in global mode); a path that does not exist simply does not detect. Every entry names why the artifact is redundant and what regenerates its replacement. Some of these act on the scope's settings.json `env` rather than on a file: `detect.settings_env_key` fires when that key is present, `detect.settings_env_value` ({key, equals}) fires only when it still holds that exact value, `rename_settings_env` ({from, to}) moves the user's VALUE to the new key and drops the old one, `remove_settings_env` ({key, when_value}) DROPS a key this stack RETIRED - nothing reads it any more, so the value is not moved anywhere; `when_value` is optional and narrows the removal to the exact value the installer itself seeded, which is what a key that still means something OUTSIDE this stack must carry, and `clear_settings_env` ({key, when_value, to}) RESETS a key whose SEEDED DEFAULT turned out to be wrong - only when the value is still that seed, so a value the user set by hand is never touched; `to` names the value it resets to (absent means empty). The installers' env pass applies the same pair on every install and update (the list is mirrored in both twins), so an env migration is REPORTED by the update command, never confirmed as a prune - nothing is deleted and a hand-set value is carried over, not reset to the default. New env keys need no entry: the installers seed them absent-only in the same pass. An entry is REMOVED from this list when the artifact it retires comes back under a new contract: `stop-contract-askuserquestion-observe-only` unwired guard-stop-contract.js's AskUserQuestion matcher because that branch DENIED mid-response; the matcher is wired again from 0.2.55 as an injection-only branch, so leaving the migration in place would have had the update unwire, in the same run, what the installer had just wired.

migrations.why: style delivery moved to the generated path-scoped project-code-style rule - the hook's injected context never reached subagent tool calls
migrations.then: re-run /project-code-style-analyzer so the replacement rule gets generated

migrations.why: every other variable this stack owns is CLAUDE_STACK_*; the docs root was the one that was not, and a bare CLAUDE_DOCS_PATH reads as a Claude Code setting rather than a stack one
migrations.then: nothing - the value moves with the key, and the hooks read the old spelling as a fallback until the rename reaches every install

migrations.why: the fresh-session gate fires on an ABSOLUTE token count per window - 150000 on a 200k window, 400000 on a 1M one, 180000 on any other or unreadable one - so a percentage of the window is not read by anything any more. It was inert at its own default on both real tiers before it was retired, and a dead key in the env block reads as a knob that still works
migrations.then: nothing - set CLAUDE_STACK_FRESH_SESSION_200K / _1M / _DEFAULT instead, or 0 on all three to turn the offer off

migrations.why: the window is the session model's row in the shipped hooks/model-windows.json, else CLAUDE_STACK_DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW; with neither, CLAUDE_STACK_FRESH_SESSION_DEFAULT applies. The key was the first resolution layer and is read by nothing now - it was also seeded 1000000 for several releases, which declared a 1M window on every install
migrations.then: nothing - the window comes from hooks/model-windows.json, with CLAUDE_STACK_DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW for an unlisted model; put the trigger you want in the three FRESH_SESSION keys

migrations.why: CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE is Claude Code's own auto-compaction trigger, not a stack setting, and the installers wrote 40 into every project - a value nobody chose. It is dropped ONLY where it still holds that seed, so a value the user set by hand is theirs and stays
migrations.then: nothing - auto-compaction returns to the harness default; set the key yourself to pin a percentage

migrations.why: the DEFAULT tier applies when the context window cannot be read at all, and 250000 sat ABOVE a 200k window entirely, so on that tier the fresh-session gate could never fire and silently did not exist. The seed is absent-only and ctxThreshold() clamps a too-large trigger only when the window is KNOWN - which by definition it is not on this tier - so no other mechanism reaches an install carrying it (measured 2026-09-12: 3 of 3 current-shape installs still on 250000). Reset ONLY where the value is still that seed; a trigger the user chose is theirs and stays
migrations.then: nothing - the next session on an unreadable window is offered the fresh-session resume at 180,000 tokens of carry

migrations.why: the product is Alfred Code from 2.0.0; every setting it owns carries its name
migrations.then: nothing - each value moves with its key, and the hooks read the old name until this runs

migrations.why: 2.0.0 cut the sentry MCP server from the stack (R26), and with it the headers helper this key told which auth mode to send - nothing reads it any more, and a dead key in the env block reads as a knob that still works. The account file's SENTRY_SLUG and SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN are the user's credentials and are left exactly where they are
migrations.then: nothing - to keep a Sentry server, add it yourself: claude mcp add --transport http --scope project sentry https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp
